neighbours.label: In English, the last word of a sentence's subject when that subject sets up a reveal (an abstract head noun like problem, goal, truth or worry, or a 'what I wanted / all I knew' clause), at the point just before 'is/was' introduces the answer. The same nouns used as objects stay near zero, and ordinary subjects that perform an action (a person or thing doing something) fire only weakly (weaker).
neighbours.short: end of a set-up subject before 'is/was' + the answer
fire: The problem is that nobody remembered to lock the back door.
Our main goal was to finish the bridge before the rains came.
The truth is, I never liked that song in the first place.
My biggest worry was that the train would leave without us.
What I wanted was a quiet weekend with no phone calls.
All I knew was that the lights had gone out across the whole street.
The real question is whether the budget can cover a second trial.
The good news is that the patient is breathing on her own again.
quiet: Nobody remembered to lock the back door, so we had a problem.
We set a clear goal before the rains came and finished the bridge.
She finally told him the truth about the song after dinner.
He shared his biggest worry with us while we waited for the train.
I wanted a quiet weekend with no phone calls.
I knew the lights had gone out across the whole street.
The committee asked a real question about the budget for a second trial.
The nurse brought good news to the family this morning.

predictions: Most fire sentences above 0.3; the action-subject near misses (committee, nurse) may reach about 0.2. Fire sentences that open with the trigger are a risk.
